title: Chapter 1 Quiz: Jupyter Notebooks in VS Code

mcqs.title: Open the practice project
mcqs.stem: You downloaded the setup practice kit and want to work on `activity01.ipynb` with its related files visible in VS Code. Which approach follows Chapter 1?

options.text: Open the notebook directly inside the ZIP viewer and leave the kit compressed.
Extract the kit and use File → Open Folder to open the extracted `stat303-setup` folder.
Move the notebook out of the kit and open only that file, leaving the related files behind.
Use File → Open Folder to open the folder containing the Python executable.

mcqs.rationale: Opening the extracted project folder keeps the notebook and related files together and visible in Explorer. The Python installation folder is not the project folder.

mcqs.title: Verify the notebook Python
mcqs.stem: You select your familiar STAT201 Python installation using Python: Select Interpreter. Your open notebook still prints an executable path belonging to a different installation. What should you do?

options.text: Assume the notebook is correct because selecting an interpreter automatically changes every open notebook kernel.
Choose whichever kernel has the highest Python version number, regardless of its path.
Install another copy of Python before checking the available notebook kernels.
Use the notebook kernel picker to select the intended environment, then rerun the cell that prints `sys.executable`.

mcqs.rationale: Workspace interpreter selection and notebook kernel selection are separate. The executable path printed by the notebook verifies which Python actually runs its cells. Chapter 1 uses a familiar existing environment, not a required new .venv.

mcqs.title: Choose the right cell type
mcqs.stem: You have a code cell that calculates the mean of three readings. You now want to add a heading and a paragraph explaining the calculation in your report. What should you use?

options.text: A Markdown cell for the heading and explanation, while keeping the calculation in a code cell.
A Python code cell containing the paragraph as ordinary text without quotes or comments.
The terminal, because text entered there automatically becomes part of the notebook.
Only a Python comment, because Markdown cells cannot display explanations alongside code.

mcqs.rationale: Markdown cells provide formatted narrative and headings. Code cells perform computations. Terminal text is not automatically saved as notebook content.

mcqs.title: Check that the notebook runs from the beginning
mcqs.stem: Your mean calculation worked, but you then deleted the earlier cell that defined `readings`. The old result is still visible. What is the best check before considering the notebook complete?

options.text: Keep the old output; a visible result proves the current cells still run successfully.
Run only the mean calculation again without restarting, since the kernel may remember `readings`.
Restart the kernel and run all remaining code cells in order; restore the missing definition if needed, then save the successfully rerun notebook.
Save and reopen without rerunning; saved output proves that every required definition is present.

mcqs.rationale: A running kernel can retain values from deleted cells, and a notebook can retain saved output. Restarting and running all cells checks that the current notebook includes the definitions it needs.

rubric.evidence: 1 point for the student name in the notebook/report; 1 point for explanations displayed as readable Markdown text. Do not require the name to appear in a particular metadata field.

2 points for visible output from the supplied environment-information cell (Python version, executable, and working directory); 2 points for a Markdown sentence identifying the selected Python installation consistently with the output. Accept the familiar working STAT201 environment; do not require .venv or any fixed Python version or path.

1 point for defining a list of three numerical readings; 2 points for computing their mean using sum() and len(); 1 point for a visible correct result for the student’s chosen values. The example readings are not mandatory.

2 points for explaining how the code computes the mean; 2 points for distinguishing the notebook document from the kernel process that executes its code and retains values. Award 1 point within each component for a partially correct explanation.

1 point for the starter notebook’s requested record of restart/run-all and reopening checks; 1 point for a readable HTML file containing the completed code and outputs without unexplained execution errors. Treat the fresh-run record as student-reported evidence, not proof of execution history.
